title: ShinyHunters data-extortion collective + the Florida DMV (FLHSMV/DAVID) extortion claim
source: Public record on ShinyHunters (2020-2025: BreachForums, the 2024 Snowflake-tenant mass data-theft wave, the 2025 Salesforce/Salesloft-Drift OAuth data-theft-extortion campaign) + breachnews.com report (2026-09-07) of a ShinyHunters extortion claim against the Florida Dept of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles (FLHSMV) DAVID database. Threat-actor + surveillance-pipeline block. HONESTY: the actor's prior campaigns are documented fact; the 2026 Florida DMV breach is a REPORTED, UNVERIFIED extortion CLAIM (FLHSMV had not confirmed at publication; the only public evidence was a single, contested screenshot); the DMV-records -> data-broker / ICE / facial-recognition pipeline is a documented pattern, with Florida-specific specifics graded.
grade: per-edge in notes (fact | reported/unverified | contested | interpretation)

edges.notes: ShinyHunters is a long-running data-theft + extortion collective (active since ~2020) closely tied to operating/administering successive BreachForums incarnations - the primary marketplace for leaked/stolen datasets (fact; membership is fluid + partly pseudonymous).

2024: ShinyHunters-linked actors ran a mass campaign against ~165 Snowflake customer tenants using stolen/infostealer credentials (no Snowflake-product flaw), hitting Ticketmaster, AT&T, Santander and others - one of the largest data-theft waves on record (fact; some activity co-attributed to UNC5537).

2025: a ShinyHunters-branded wave used voice-phishing + abused OAuth tokens (incl. the Salesloft 'Drift' integration) to exfiltrate data from many companies' Salesforce instances, then extort them - a shift to SaaS-integration + social-engineering theft (fact).

ShinyHunters overlaps the loose English-speaking cybercrime milieu 'The Com' (which also spawned Scattered Spider + LAPSUS$); 2025 saw joint 'Scattered LAPSUS$ Hunters' branding - graded, since attribution across these fluid crews is uncertain (contested).

2026-09-07 (reported/unverified): ShinyHunters posted an extortion CLAIM to have breached FLHSMV's DAVID (Driver And Vehicle Information Database) - driver's-license data, license photo + signature, address + vehicle records - setting a 2026-09-11 contact deadline. FLHSMV had NOT confirmed any breach at publication; the only public proof was a single DAVID screenshot (a Jeffrey Epstein record) whose authenticity/provenance is contested (could derive from prior investigative disclosures). A possible tie to a larger 'Nexus' 153M+ license-record dataset was floated but unconfirmed.

FLHSMV operates DAVID - the state portal exposing Floridians' driver + vehicle records (license data, photo, signature, address, vehicle history) to authorized law-enforcement + agency users; a high-value single-point repository of resident identity data (fact).

State DMV driver records + license photos have been accessed by federal immigration enforcement (ICE/HSI), including facial-recognition searches of DMV photo databases - documented nationally; the Florida-specific access scope is graded (fact of the general pattern; FL specifics contested).

US state DMVs have sold/shared motor-vehicle records with data brokers + private buyers under DPPA 'permissible use' carve-outs, feeding the commercial identity-data economy; a DMV breach collapses that same dataset into the criminal market (fact of the national pattern; FL-specific practice graded).

DMV license-photo databases are a core enrollment source for government + commercial facial recognition (the largest de-facto biometric databases of ordinary residents) - making a DMV compromise a biometric-exposure event, not just a PII one (fact of category; specific FL use graded).

ShinyHunters exemplifies the pivot from encryption-ransomware to pure data-theft extortion ('exfiltrate + name-and-shame + pay-or-leak'), the dominant e-crime model - distinct from but adjacent to the RaaS ecosystem (interpretation of category).
